craft_claim: Understatement and hyperbole work by violating register or scale expectations, and wordplay works by activating an unexpected second sense of a word or phrase that then resolves.

supporting_evidence.note: Register and scale clashes are a species of incongruity; Bergson's account of the comic supports framing understatement and hyperbole as controlled expectation-violations.
Wordplay fits the two-stage model: the phrase sets one expectation, the second sense violates it, and the resolution yields the comic effect.
Observable technique: mock-formal narration and mixed-register diction set up scale clashes that resolve as wordplay; described, not quoted.

counterevidence.note: Section G 'Bathos' records that the same low-register move that is comic when intended becomes bathos when it collides with stakes the text is trying to honour; with section B's Bergson condition that laughter requires an absence of feeling, register violation is framing-dependent and can sabotage a serious passage instead of amusing.

scope: Prose and copy at the sentence and phrase level.
exceptions: Wordplay that depends on a specific language's homophones does not survive translation and must not be claimed cross-linguistically.
